name: Sleaford Mods
label: Rough Trade
lede: Jason Williamson was a 43-year-old benefits adviser for Nottingham City Council when people started listening: one man ranting in an East Midlands accent over Andrew Fearn's laptop loops, on a label run by a city bus driver.

hero.by: Williamson and Fearn, July 2015. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Pyjamas, a Mars bar and a Roni Size loop
eras.text: Williamson spent his twenties and thirties failing at music in Grantham, San Francisco and Nottingham, and sliding from job to job. Then a friend put his words over somebody else's beat, and the failing became the subject.

years.h: A song about buying a Mars bar in his pyjamas starts it all
years.p: Broke, Williamson writes 'Teacher Faces Porn Charges' about going to the shop in his pyjamas for a Mars bar and a can of Special Brew. His friend [[Simon Parfrement|9d4956c3-1aca-46df-88df-52cca6384fcd]] suggests putting it over a loop from a Roni Size record.
years.xp:
Before this, Williamson spent nine months in San Francisco looking for bandmates, then sang in a string of Nottingham groups. One late-Britpop band was nearly called Sunday Dinner before settling on Meat Pie; the plan was Small Faces crossed with Guns N' Roses. "Meat Pie finished 'cos I got into sniff," he told the Guardian.

The Parfrement experiment "worked, straight away," Williamson said. "It was better than anything I'd ever done." He was by then doing agency jobs and getting sacked from them, and taking what he called mental snapshots of every time he fell lower.

years.h: That's Shit, Try Harder becomes Sleaford Mods
years.p: The project's first name doesn't last. The new one comes from Sleaford, a Lincolnshire town 15 miles from Williamson's hometown of Grantham, and the mod scene he joined as a pre-teen [[The Jam|23228f18-01d5-493e-94ce-cfcde82a8db2]] fan.
years.xp:
Williamson and Parfrement record with an engineer at Rubber Biscuit Studio in Nottingham. The first two albums, Sleaford Mods and The Mekon, come out in 2007 on A52 Sounds as CDs and downloads, pressed up piecemeal.

His modern touchstones: a work colleague had turned him on to the [[Wu-Tang Clan|0febdcf7-4e1f-4661-9493-b40427de2c13]], and The Streets' Original Pirate Material made his ears prick up.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sleaford Mods · The Guardian (2014) · LeftLion
years.h: Fearn DJs his own grime tracks at the Chameleon, and Williamson listens
years.p: At a small Nottingham club called the Chameleon, Williamson hears [[Andrew Fearn|701b4172-039a-43d5-8b7e-a81b67bd4561]] playing his own rough, minimal tracks. The Chameleon is also where Steve Underwood, a bus driver with a noise label, first hears Williamson.
years.xp:
Fearn, a farm kid from Saxilby, had spent four and a half years cold-calling people about gym memberships ("Mainly calling old people who could barely walk"). He'd already seen Williamson perform: "Friends of mine hated it. They didn't know how to take this shouty man."

Underwood remembered sitting in the corner at the Chameleon, taken with the samples of [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]] and Conflict and the lines about Nottingham pubs and clubs.

eras.title: Two men, a laptop and a bus driver's label
eras.text: Fearn took over the music and stripped it to bass, drums and loops. Underwood's Harbinger Sound, bankrolled from bus-driving wages, pressed the records, and the UK caught up with what Germany already knew.

years.h: Wank is Fearn's first album; Parfrement steps back
years.p: Parfrement hands the music over to Fearn after Wank. He stays on as the band's photographer and media producer.

years.h: Austerity Dogs: 300 copies, stamped Made in Nottingham
years.p: Underwood had planned a seven-inch and ended up with an album. Norman Records, the mail-order shop, made it its album of the year.
years.xp:
Underwood started Harbinger Sound in 1992; its first release was the Japanese noise artist Pain Jerk. He ran it on noise, punk and avant-garde records, paid for by 14-hour days as a spare driver for Nottingham City Transport.

"If I can do it anyone can do it," he told LeftLion. "There is no black art to it."

years.h: Germany goes mad for them before England does
years.p: Fearn told the Guardian that in Germany "people go fucking mad." Their regular Hamburg hotel, and the smell of its toilet, ended up in the opening line of 'Tied Up in Nottz'.
years.xp: Williamson made sure a photo of the toilet in question was tweeted. "It still smells the same," he said. "Terrible."

years.src: Wikipedia: Divide and Exit · Wikipedia: Sleaford Mods
years.h: Divide and Exit lands in the Guardian's top ten of 2014
years.p: Fourteen songs, recorded at Arro Nottz and Rubber Biscuit. It reaches No. 2 on the UK indie chart, and 'Fizzy' goes top 15 on the physical singles chart.

q: This music was born out of a hate for pretenders like you.
years.h: Miles Kane follows them on Twitter. Williamson tells him off
years.p: Kane had praised the band and tried to follow them. Williamson's reply, which he showed the Guardian on his phone in a Caffè Nero, told Kane exactly what he thought of retro rock.
years.xp: Kane wasn't the only target. Kasabian, Oasis and a former member of Candy Flip all turn up in the songs or on the band's feed. Asked whether the words show what it's like in his head, Williamson said: "The rage? Yeah. That's why Sleaford Mods is. Definitely."

years.cap: Sleaford Mods at the Palace, St. Gallen, Switzerland, May 2014
years.h: Williamson quits the council; Underwood quits the buses
years.p: Williamson leaves his job as a benefits adviser to go professional. Underwood drives his last bus the day before a Rescue Rooms gig in Nottingham.
years.xp: Underwood had driven for Nottingham City Transport for 13 or 14 years, covering school runs and night routes so he'd have time for the label.

years.h: Williamson publishes his lyrics as Grammar Wanker
years.p: The first book of his words, covering 2007 to 2014. A second, Jason Williamson's House Party, follows in 2019.

years.h: The Prodigy put them on The Day Is My Enemy
years.p: The track is 'Ibiza', announced at the end of 2014. In June, Leftfield's first album in 16 years carries 'Head and Shoulders' with Williamson.

years.cap: Williamson and Fearn on stage, July 2015
years.h: Key Markets shows up between Tamla Motown and Universal
years.p: The album goes in at No. 9 on the midweek chart and settles at 11. Underwood couldn't get over seeing Harbinger Sound wedged between the majors.
years.xp: It's one of 19 records shortlisted for the IMPALA Album of the Year Award. The same year the duo are the subject of the documentary Sleaford Mods: Invisible Britain.

years.h: Channel 4 News asks them about Corbyn and poverty
years.p: Williamson and Fearn sit down with Channel 4 News to talk about Jeremy Corbyn, poverty and the way people speak.

eras.title: In and out of Rough Trade
eras.text: The duo signed to Rough Trade, made a post-Brexit record in the studio of Pulp's Steve Mackey and toured North America. Then they left, and parted with Steve Underwood, the manager whose label had made their name.

years.cap: Sleaford Mods at Haldern Pop festival, Germany
years.h: Labour suspends Williamson's membership
years.p: The party cites online abuse and bars him from voting in the leadership election. Williamson answers on Twitter, calling the party "absolute scum" for taking a year of his money.

years.h: Rough Trade's first Sleaford Mods record is the T.C.R. EP
years.p: They leave Harbinger Sound for Rough Trade. Harbinger still puts out Live at SO36, recorded in Berlin, that November.

years.src: Wikipedia: English Tapas · Wikipedia: Sleaford Mods
years.h: English Tapas goes in at No. 12
years.p: Recorded at Steve Mackey's West Heath studios in London, it's mostly about England after the EU referendum. The band follow it with their first North American tour.

years.h: Bunch of Kunst, Christine Franz's film about them, opens
years.p: The Guardian's review headline says the film rips austerity Britain a fresh one.

q: In hindsight, we left too early.
years.src: PopMatters · XS Noize · Clash · Wikipedia: Sleaford Mods
years.h: Out of Rough Trade, then out goes the manager
years.p: A self-titled EP in September is their last Rough Trade release for now. Williamson later said Underwood had pushed them to go independent, calling labels dinosaurs.
years.xp:
The duo set up their own label, Extreme Eating. Speaking to XS Noize, Williamson said Rough Trade gave them "an excellent infrastructure and we learned from that."

To PopMatters he was blunter: going independent was premature, and "we should have waited at least a year." They parted with Underwood and built a new team.

years.src: NME: IDLES · Happy Mag · NME: class
years.h: Williamson says IDLES are appropriating a working-class voice
years.p: He tells the Guardian he doesn't like IDLES at all. Joe Talbot replies there's no authenticity "in just being a prick to everyone." The two make up on Talbot's podcast in 2025.
years.xp:
Williamson called IDLES' take "cliched, patronising, insulting and mediocre." He kept at the theme in 2021, telling NME he wouldn't pose in front of a high-rise.

By 2025 he'd been in therapy to rein in the confrontations, and on Talbot's Oh Gatekeeper podcast Talbot called him "an old and new friend."

years.h: Eton Alive, the first record on their own label
years.p: Recorded at JT Soar in Nottingham and released on Extreme Eating, it reaches No. 9 and tops the indie chart. Williamson is three years sober, and the songs move away from the pub.
years.xp: "I've been three years sober, and it's like other things come into play," Williamson told PopMatters. One song grew out of a dealer having a fit outside his house.

years.h: Glastonbury, late on a Saturday night
years.p: Williamson and Fearn play the festival on Saturday, June 29, four months after Eton Alive topped the indie chart.

eras.title: Number one on vinyl, number three on the chart
eras.text: Back on Rough Trade, the duo started letting other voices in, and every album climbed higher than the last. The rants stayed; the guest list got longer.

years.h: All That Glue marks the return to Rough Trade
years.p: A compilation of their run so far, it reaches No. 10.

yt: 'Mork n Mindy' ft. Billy Nomates, official video
years.h: 'Mork n Mindy', with Billy Nomates, tops the vinyl singles chart
years.p: Billy Nomates sings with Williamson, and the film director Ben Wheatley makes the video.

years.cap: Sleaford Mods at South Facing Festival, Crystal Palace Bowl, London, August 2021
years.h: Spare Ribs gets five stars from NME and reaches No. 4
years.p: Amy Taylor of Amyl and the Sniffers guests on 'Nudge It'. NME says there's "nowhere to hide."

years.h: Williamson plays Lazarus in the Peaky Blinders finale
years.p: A cameo in the last episode of the BBC series. In October the band appear on [[Orbital|f3e2a7d9-c6bb-4848-95e5-04c0a1e2f511]]'s 'Dirty Rat'.

years.h: UK Grim hits No. 3, their highest yet
years.p: Recorded at JT Soar, produced by Fearn. Florence Shaw of [[Dry Cleaning|8a74e5ea-6f68-49e1-951c-80d2291f7c3f]] is on 'Force 10 from Navarone'; Perry Farrell and Dave Navarro of [[Jane's Addiction|e3434cc7-d348-491a-9dc8-325af3d9086d]] are on 'So Trendy'.

years.h: A scarf thrown twice on stage ends the Madrid show
years.p: During 'Nudge It' at La Riviera, a Palestinian scarf lands on stage. Williamson throws it back with a warning; it comes back and the band walk off.
years.xp: Williamson posted: "Don't be asking me to pick sides for something I ain't got any real idea about, at a gig. I'm a singer. My job is music." He added that he was "sick and tired of premature death like we all are," and clarified his position on Palestine a week later.

years.h: Their 'West End Girls' cover goes top ten
years.p: The [[Pet Shop Boys|be540c02-7898-4b79-9acc-c8122c7d9e83]] song, on the More UK Grim EP, reaches No. 9 on the UK sales chart.

eras.title: Therapy, then Planet X
eras.text: Williamson went to therapy for the anger he'd made a career of and patched things up with old targets. The music kept its teeth, and the duo's thirteenth album brought in actors and singer-songwriters.

years.h: Two songs with Hot Chip for War Child
years.p: 'Nom Nom Nom' and 'Cat Burglar' raise money for the children's charity.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sleaford Mods · Louder Than War
years.h: Gwendoline Christie is on the new single
years.p: 'The Good Life' features Midlands duo Big Special and the actress, and opens the next album.

years.cap: Jason Williamson at SXSW London, June 2026
years.src: NME: Demise · Louder Than War · Wikipedia: Sleaford Mods
years.h: The Demise of Planet X: Aldous Harding, Sue Tompkins, Snowy
years.p: Thirteen songs, five with guests including [[Aldous Harding|1d779dfd-d292-48b5-b232-a09687b9881a]] and Life Without Buildings' Sue Tompkins. It reaches No. 6 and tops the indie chart.
years.xp:
Williamson told NME the record drew on "October 7, then the genocide, this new wave of nationalism in this country," unfinished business from Covid, and "the rot that is social media."

The review noted he'd stopped going after other musicians since making peace with IDLES' Joe Talbot. Nottingham singer Liam Bailey and the rapper Snowy round out the guests.
